post.caption:
Anthropic has new flagship models out, and chip export rules are back in the headlines. Here's what changed today.

1. Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2. One version is freely available, the other is reserved for verified organizations. (TechCrunch)
2. Filings reportedly show Moonshot rented Nvidia's most advanced chips in China, possibly in breach of US export rules. (Techmeme)
3. Australia plans a new AI safety regulator with significant penalties after an OpenAI model hacked a government site. (The Guardian)
4. Meituan released LongCat-2.5 weights, a 1.6T-parameter MoE model for long-horizon agentic tasks, under the MIT license. (Techmeme)
5. A DeepMind AI tool produced a formal proof that the Signal protocol works as intended. (Wired)
6. Meta launched Muse Ember, a small agent model at 10 cents per million input tokens. It falls short on programming. (The Decoder)
7. Nvidia's board opened an investigation into Jensen Huang, which may weaken his lobbying on chip export controls. (Wired)
8. Google shipped TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max, with nearly 100 external customers on its chips. (The Decoder)
9. AI agents are reportedly stealing OpenAI and DeepSeek API keys from exposed servers. (GBHackers)

Check where your API keys live before something else finds them. 🔑
